accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:polynomial-oracle-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The lower half and its no-dyadic-loss formulation are conditional on a favourable resolution of oeq:sequential-multiscale-certificate.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The matched all-policy frontier is a downstream conditional consequence of the certificate, while the certificate itself remains the sole root solve target.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher landing page and abstract; corroborating author manuscript, Abstract and Sections 3 and 7
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper formulates minimax switchback-design optimization under assumptions on a finite carryover order and supplies inference and misspecification analyses; it does not state an all-feedback fixed-array polynomial-memory converse.

The paper assumes geometrically mixing Markov dynamics and obtains GATE/FATE error guarantees using regular switchbacks and burn-in; its stochastic model is not the proposed deterministic historical-envelope class.

The paper studies graph-spatial interference with rapidly mixing MDP temporal interference and gives truncated-HT near-optimal MSE rates, not an all-policy one-unit fixed-array polynomial-memory lower bound.
The result is a general constrained-risk inequality for two distributions and arbitrary non-decreasing losses; it supplies no switchback occupancy or adaptive-trajectory construction.

Sequential rerandomization balances prespecified prognostic variables from past observations, treats no carryover and extends to first-order carryover; it does not prove a polynomial-memory minimax converse.

The paper studies adaptive efficient design for estimating the steady-state reward difference of unknown Markov chains via maximum likelihood, which is orthogonal to adversarial fixed potential-outcome arrays.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the common-null occupancy--information inequality a separately named theorem with explicit dyadic aggregation constants, so a possible logarithmic loss is isolated rather than absorbed into the final frontier.

Add a short formal non-subsumption comparison against Lin--Ding's decaying-carryover regression setting and the published regular-design classes, identifying the all-feedback policy quantifier and fixed-array envelope as the two strict differences.
After the certificate is resolved, add a finite-horizon corollary giving the exact admissible range of T for L_T<=T/4 and the resulting implementable design rule.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the sequential multiscale common-null certificate as the sole root target; retain the matched frontier only as its explicitly conditional downstream consequence.
